title: Next.js Data Access and i18n: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on querying databases from Server Components with Prisma or Drizzle, reusing connections in development, keeping DB code server-only, and i18n routing with a [lang] segment, middleware and dictionaries.

chapters.title: Server-Side Data Access: The Mental Model
points: Server Components are async functions: await the DB call directly in the component body, with no API route and no useEffect
DB code runs only on the server, so credentials and queries never reach the client bundle
Fetch where the data is used; the result is serialised into the RSC payload, so only plain serialisable values can be passed to Client Components
Dynamic rendering follows when a component reads request data (cookies, headers); otherwise the DB query runs at build time and the page is static
Independent queries should run in parallel with Promise.all; sequential awaits create a waterfall

chapters.title: Prisma and Drizzle Workflow
points: Prisma: define models in schema.prisma, run prisma generate to build the typed client, then query with prisma.user.findMany()
Prisma schema changes: prisma migrate dev in development, prisma migrate deploy in production
Drizzle: define tables in TypeScript with pgTable, query with db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, id))
Drizzle migrations: drizzle-kit generate creates SQL, drizzle-kit migrate applies it; drizzle-kit push syncs the schema directly for prototyping
Prisma vs Drizzle: Prisma has a generated client and its own schema language; Drizzle is SQL-like, schema in TS, lighter at runtime

chapters.title: Connection Reuse in Development
points: Hot reload re-runs module code, so each reload creates a new PrismaClient and a new connection pool
Symptom: too many connections errors from the database during next dev
Fix: cache the client on globalThis and reuse it if it exists
Only cache outside production: if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma
Drizzle with a driver such as postgres or pg needs the same globalThis caching; serverless drivers over HTTP do not

chapters.title: Keeping DB Code Server-Only
points: import 'server-only' makes the build fail if a Client Component imports the module
Put DB access in a data access layer (lib/data.ts) and import only that from components
Only NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars reach the browser; DATABASE_URL must never carry that prefix
Return DTOs with only the needed fields, not whole rows, so sensitive columns such as password hashes are not passed to the client
Server Actions are public endpoints: re-check authentication and authorisation inside each one

chapters.title: i18n Routing with [lang] and Dictionaries
points: Put pages under app/[lang]/ so the locale is a dynamic segment; read it from the params prop
Middleware reads the Accept-Language header, negotiates a locale from the supported list, and redirects paths with no locale to /en/...
Middleware matcher must exclude _next, static files and api routes, otherwise assets get redirected
Dictionaries are JSON files per locale loaded with dynamic import: import(`./${lang}.json`).then(m => m.default)
Wrap the loader in server-only; call getDictionary(lang) in Server Components and pass strings down as props; in recent Next.js versions params is a Promise and must be awaited
Add generateStaticParams to return the supported locales so each language pre-renders

chapters.title: Data Access and i18n Cheat Sheet
points: Server Component query: const rows = await db.select().from(t); no API layer needed
Prisma commands: prisma generate, prisma migrate dev, prisma migrate deploy
Drizzle commands: drizzle-kit generate, drizzle-kit migrate, drizzle-kit push
Dev singleton: globalThis.prisma ?? new PrismaClient(), cached only when NODE_ENV is not production
Guards: import 'server-only', no NEXT_PUBLIC_ on secrets, return DTOs, re-check auth in Server Actions
i18n: app/[lang]/, middleware redirect with matcher exclusions, getDictionary(lang) via dynamic import, generateStaticParams for locales
